name: Vancomycin
executiveSummary: Glycopeptide against gram-positives (MRSA, enterococci). Usual adult **15–20 mg/kg IV every 8–12 h** (load 25–30 mg/kg in severe disease). Pediatrics 40–60 mg/kg/day. Infuse ≥ 60 min; monitor trough/AUC.
indications:
## Indications

- Severe beta-lactam–resistant gram-positive infections (MRSA, enterococci, etc.): bacteremia, endocarditis, osteomyelitis, nosocomial pneumonia, meningitis, septic arthritis.
- Selected surgical prophylaxis (implants, beta-lactam allergy).
- *C. difficile* colitis: **PO** (not IV for luminal disease).

## Precautions

- Rapid infusion → red-man syndrome / hypotension.
- Nephro- and ototoxicity; adjust in renal failure; irritant on extravasation.
- Orientative trough targets: **10–15 µg/mL** non-severe; **15–20 µg/mL** bacteremia/endocarditis/osteomyelitis/meningitis/MRSA pneumonia (or AUC/MIC per modern protocol).

> Never IV push. Separate from ceftriaxone in the same line.

adulto.presentation: Vial 500–1000 mg; PO capsules for *C. difficile*.
adulto.dose: IV: **15–20 mg/kg every 8–12 h** (actual body weight; round to 250 mg). Severe infections: load **25–30 mg/kg** (usual max **2 g**), then maintenance. Surgical prophylaxis: **15 mg/kg** (usual **1–1.5 g**) 30–120 min before incision. *C. difficile* PO: **125 mg every 6 h** × 10 days (severe: up to **500 mg every 6 h** per guideline).
adulto.administration: Reconstitute with sterile water; dilute to ≤ **5 mg/mL** in NS; infuse **≥ 60 min** (90–120 min if dose > 1 g). PO only for colitis.
adulto.notes: Trough monitoring from ~48 h or earlier if renal failure/instability.

pediatrico.dose: Other infections: **40 mg/kg/day every 6–8 h**. Sepsis/bacteremia/meningitis/arthritis: **60 mg/kg/day every 6 h**. CF: often **60–80 mg/kg/day** by center. Max aligned to adult per dose.
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight; levels per pediatric protocol.

neonatal.dose: By postmenstrual age and creatinine (e.g. 10–15 mg/kg every 8–24–48 h) — follow NNU table.
neonatal.notes: Long intervals in preterms; monitoring essential.

stability:
## Stability

- Dilution: per label; typically 24 h refrigerated in NS.
- Do not mix with beta-lactams/heparin in the same syringe.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Red-man syndrome, phlebitis, nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, neutropenia, rash, drug fever.
